WSR metrics from AI Platform Build (same engagement, similar team structure) show PR abandon rate increasing to 31.6%, average cycle time 6.19 days with one PR at 25.8 days, and PRs being broken into smaller units. Historical Risk R05 (Code Quality Concerns) shows similar pattern of quality issues under dependency churn and mid-sprint changes. With testing phases at 0% and compressed timeline, quality issues may not be discovered until production.
triggerConditions: Production defects discovered during Go-Live or early Hypercare
Performance or stability issues surface under production load
Technical debt from rushed implementation requires emergency fixes
Defect rate during Hypercare exceeds team resolution capacity
Customer-facing issues require escalation and emergency patches

potentialImpact.quality: Production defects requiring emergency fixes during Hypercare; Technical debt accumulation requiring post-Hypercare remediation
potentialImpact.operations: Increased incident rate during Hypercare; Operational instability affecting producer experience
potentialImpact.customer: Customer confidence eroded by production issues; Hypercare escalation and relationship risk

predictedRisks.reasoning: This risk has medium likelihood because the project exhibits the same quality pressure signals identified in historical intelligence: strong velocity but increasing PR abandon rates, elevated cycle times, and PR rework. Historical Risk R05 shows code quality concerns arose under similar conditions (dependency churn, mid-sprint changes), and the mitigation (strengthened code review) did not fully address upstream causes. With testing phases at 0% and only 39 days to contract end, the compressed timeline creates pressure to maintain velocity, potentially at the expense of quality. However, the likelihood is medium rather than high because the project has strong quality controls (SAST, SCA, unit tests, automation, regression pipeline) and positive stakeholder feedback. The impact is medium because quality issues are more likely to surface during Hypercare (when mitigation is possible) rather than causing Go-Live failure.

actions: Strengthen code review rigor with mandatory peer review for all PRs, automated quality gate enforcement (SonarQube, JFrog Xray, Snyk), and root cause analysis for abandoned or long-cycle PRs to prevent technical debt accumulation
Establish Hypercare incident response process with severity-based resolution SLAs, daily defect triage, and escalation protocol for customer-facing issues to maintain operational stability

recommendations.Quality Monitoring: Track PR quality metrics (abandon rate, cycle time, rework patterns) as leading indicators of technical debt and quality pressure, with corrective action if abandon rate exceeds 20 percent
recommendations.Technical Debt Management: Reserve 20 percent of Hypercare capacity for technical debt remediation and post-production defect resolution to prevent operational instability
recommendations.Defect Prevention: Conduct pre-Go-Live code quality review of high-risk modules (Book of Business, Dashboard, Authentication) to identify and remediate technical debt before production deployment

predictedRisks.responseRationale: Historical Risk R05 shows code quality concerns arose under dependency churn and mid-sprint changes, with mitigation addressing review hygiene but not upstream causes. Historical pattern 'Accelerating Velocity with Quality Trade-offs' has 0.85 confidence and MEDIUM impact. Current evidence shows increasing PR abandon rates and elevated cycle times. Strengthened quality controls and Hypercare capacity reservation are required to prevent post-Go-Live escalation.
